note: Founding members of Foundation0. No pictures by design. Names as each member shows them on GitHub or in their own published work.

members.name: Ahraz Arifuddin
members.summary: Runs Aska Digital's team of AI agents and points it at open questions. The main project follows a childhood doodle (a square, its diagonals, one dot per triangle) into crystal geometry, ending in an exact proof that a loose ball-and-rod scaffold folds, without stretching, into the densest stacking of equal balls.

work.name: Incentre lattice
work.note: Exact fold from density 0.2233 to 0.7405 (the Kepler bound), with 16,240 exact certificate coefficients.

work.name: Exoplanets: pipeline fixes and website
work.note: Ten merged pull requests to eumemic's search: four pipeline fixes, one of which (PR #6) led to a re-search that added 120 counted candidates; an independent check; tests; documentation; and the first version of the project website.

work.name: mobius-x1: full-network check
work.note: The whole-network test behind Theorem 2: 0 failures in 3,456,000 checks.

work.name: gf2m-circuits: field multipliers
work.note: Verified multiplier circuits for more binary fields, e.g. GF(2^9) in 136 gates against a 142 baseline.

work.name: Foundation0
work.note: Began as a live tracker of the integer-multiplication race.

members.name: eumemic
members.summary: Builds software for long-running AI agents and puts those agents to work on open science. The main project, built with Claude Code, searched NASA's public TESS data for more than four million stars and as of 14 October 2026 counts 665 small-planet candidates too faint to see in any single month of data.

work.name: Exoplanets
work.note: 4,039,203 stars searched; 665 candidates as of 14 Oct 2026.

work.name: Integer-multiplication race
work.note: 80 of the first 722 pull requests inventoried in the race's PR ledger (13 Oct 2026); on 13 Oct the record's bit block built on their #555.

work.name: exact-dft-bounds
work.note: Exact Fourier transforms below n log n with saving 4.856×10⁻⁴; held the best claim for about six hours.

work.name: rlmath
work.note: A test bench for training an AI to split Lean theorems into lemmas a smaller prover can finish.

members.name: Doug Colkitt
members.summary: Started and maintains the open race to multiply huge numbers in fewer than n log n steps, the best speed proven so far. People and their AI agents took a machine-written paper's saving of 2^−182 and grew it to about 2^−9.2 in a week, every step checked in exact arithmetic, all still resting on the unreviewed original paper.

work.name: integer-mult-bounds
work.note: Creator and maintainer; κ from 2^−182 to 0.00167266 (PR #1094, 13 Oct 2026).

work.name: erdos-875-carry-lemmas
work.note: One model proves, a rival model attacks: a sharp carry lemma behind the best construction for Erdős Problem 875. Not a resolution of the problem.

work.name: Gradients to ChatGPT (g2c)
work.note: A build-it-yourself course on how language models work.

members.name: rohanarun
members.summary: Builds software that lets AI coding agents work on open research problems, including Auto-research-agent, a Mac app that sends Codex or Claude Code to an open problem in one click. With those agents, the most active contributor to the integer-multiplication race, and the author of conditional refinements to four of OpenAI's machine-written papers.

work.name: Auto-research-agent
work.note: A native Mac app: one click sends your own coding agent, or several in parallel, to an open problem.

work.name: Integer-multiplication race
work.status: Reviewed record on 13–14 Oct 2026 · conditional · maintainer-reviewed
work.note: 142 pull requests as of 14 Oct 2026; PR #1094 was the reviewed record on 13–14 Oct 2026 (κ = 0.001672660197076918).

work.name: van-der-waerden-refinement
work.note: The constant in OpenAI's van der Waerden bound rose from 1/100000 to 1/9, jointly with other contributors.

work.name: sidorenko-template-refinements
work.note: No smaller certificate than OpenAI's 35-vertex counterexample exists inside its template; one constant cut from 1641 to 189.

work.name: matrix-multiplication-sector-barrier
work.status: Proof + exact tests · not peer reviewed
work.note: Shows where one step of OpenAI's 9/4 matrix-multiplication method must stop.

work.name: unit-distance-grid-refinement
work.note: Shrinks the final grid in OpenAI's unit-distance proof from 20×5 to 8×4.

work.name: integer-multiplication-illustrated
work.note: An illustrated reading guide and annotated edition of OpenAI's integer-multiplication paper.

members.name: Ryan Shea
members.summary: Builds tools for AI-run experiments, such as autofoundry, which rents GPUs from four cloud providers and runs the same experiment across them. Working with Codex and Claude on OpenAI's machine-written problems, they ranked first, as of 14 Oct 2026, on a public board for exact Fourier transforms below n log n, with a Lean-verified result shared with Jeremy Kothe, whose circuit it uses.

work.name: autofoundry
work.note: Rents GPUs across RunPod, Vast.ai, PRIME Intellect and Lambda, runs one experiment everywhere, reports best, mean and worst.

work.name: fourier-transform-below-nlogn
work.note: Exact Fourier transforms of any length in O(n (log n)^(1−δ)) steps with δ = 0.0012331685; rank 1 on the Big O Speedrun board as of 14 Oct 2026, shared with Jeremy Kothe.

work.name: matroid-prophet-inequality
work.status: Written proof + exact certificates · not reviewed
work.note: Raises a guaranteed fraction in the one-sample matroid prophet problem from 2^−293 to above (35/32)·2^−31.
